title: Install a graphics card in a PC case (Franka, operational-space control)
text:
A gaming-PC case lying on its side on a sturdy table, opening up, its motherboard facing the ceiling. The board's primary PCIe x16 slot is empty, and the rear I/O panel has an open expansion-slot cutout. Beside the case a loose graphics card stands upright in a foam holder, already in its installation orientation.
Goal: grip the card by its top edge, lift it straight out of the holder, lower it into the case with its I/O bracket just forward of the rear panel, slide it rearward until the bracket and ports pass through the cutout, line its PCB edge connector up with the x16 slot, and press it straight down until it bottoms out. A seated card stays put on its own. The task is complete once the card is fully seated. The card holds in a firm pinch: close the fingers squarely across its body slab near the top edge and the grip locks; open wide to release.
success: Success, exactly: at the end of the run, the graphics card sits in the motherboard's PCIe x16 slot so that, in the fixed case's frame (board face horizontal, facing up), the bottom-centre of the card's gold edge-connector tab is at most 4.5 mm above the board face, i.e. at least 4 mm below the slot mouth 8.5 mm above the face (it bottoms out at 3.5 mm), and within 3 mm horizontally of its fully seated position; the card's up axis (edge connector to top edge) is within 3° of the board normal and its length axis within 3° of the seated heading, which is the heading it already has standing in the foam holder at the start. Not true at the start (the card is in its holder beside the case). [scene.seated(); seated tab point world (0.48405, 0.0293, 0.0324); board face z 0.0289]
